findings.userImpact: Any case writer (MEMBER, assigned INVESTIGATOR) can remove a held record from the held case via Remove from case, bulk REMOVE_FROM_CASE or matter-workspace unlink; afterwards the record is no longer held and can be trashed, and later destroyed by retention.
findings.legalImpact: Defeats a preservation obligation: a case-scoped legal hold covers exactly the records currently linked, and linkage is mutable by non-admins with no hold check. Case deletion is refused under the same hold precisely because it detaches links, so the gap is inconsistent with the platform's own rule.
findings.securityImpact: Within-tenant integrity/preservation bypass; no cross-tenant access.
findings.reproduction: 1) Workspace case C with linked evidence E; place an ACTIVE hold scope=CASE caseId=C. 2) As a MEMBER: DELETE /v1/cases/C/evidence/E (or POST /v1/evidence/bulk {action:REMOVE_FROM_CASE}, or DELETE /v1/cases/C/evidence-links/:linkId). 3) Returns 200; case_evidence_links row deleted. 4) evaluateEffectiveLegalHold(E) now resolves no linked case -> not held; POST trash on E succeeds.
findings.observed: detachEvidenceFromCase deletes the link row with no hold evaluation; none of its three callers evaluates holds. evaluateCaseDeletionHold is used only for case DELETE.
findings.expected: Detaching evidence from a case that carries an ACTIVE CASE hold (or while the evidence is otherwise held via that case) is refused (403 LEGAL_HOLD_BLOCKED, fail-closed 503 when hold state unreadable), inside the one detach authority so no caller can skip it.
findings.rootCause: The case-hold scope is computed dynamically from mutable links (resolveLinkedCaseIds), but the one detach authority treats linkage as a pure relationship edit and has no preservation gate.
findings.remediation: In detachEvidenceFromCase (and detachAllEvidenceFromCase) evaluate ACTIVE holds with scope=CASE for caseId (and historical holds) inside the transaction, fail closed; map to 403 in cases.routes, case-workspace and bulk. Alternatively snapshot case-hold membership at hold placement.
findings.requiredTests: Integration: CASE hold active -> single, bulk and case-workspace unlink all refused with zero mutation; hold store unreadable -> 503 zero mutation; after hold release unlink succeeds; trash after refused unlink still blocked.

findings.title: The app cannot stop the iOS broadcast: in-app Stop and every controlled stop post a Darwin note the extension never observes, then return a fabricated INTERRUPTED summary while recording continues

findings.userImpact: Tapping 'Stop & Review' (or hitting the byte ceiling / upload backpressure) does not stop recording: the status-bar indicator stays on and the extension keeps writing up to 600 segments into the container. The review shows 'Interrupted' for a session the user ended cleanly; everything recorded after the tap is never emitted or uploaded and is wiped at the next start.
findings.legalImpact: The sealed manifest (if it could seal) would state INTERRUPTED_SESSION/terminationReason INTERRUPTED with captureStartedAtUtc equal to the stop instant and totalDurationMs 0 — false provenance for a clean stop. The client byte/backpressure bounds (SESSION_BOUNDS_REACHED, SEGMENT_UPLOAD_BACKPRESSURE) are unenforceable on iOS.
findings.securityImpact: Recording of the screen continues after the user asked PROOVRA to stop (OS indicator remains visible; user can still stop from Control Center).
findings.reproduction: stopContinuousCapture (Swift :97-105) posts com.proovra.screencapture.ios.finished (:100). SampleHandler registers no Darwin observer at all (whole file; it only POSTS at :136 and :152), so the broadcast keeps running. The app's own observer for that same name (:119-123) fires, emitting onScreenContinuousStopped with readResult(); readResult finds no result.json (the extension only writes it in broadcastFinished/stopBroadcast, SampleHandler.swift:75,86) and returns the fallback (ProovraBroadcastShared.swift:136-143): startedAtUtc=endedAtUtc=now, totalDurationMs 0, INTERRUPTED. stopObserving (:103) then removes the handlers, so later segments are never emitted. requestControlledStop (continuous-capture.tsx:105-113) uses the same call.
findings.observed: One-way IPC (extension→app only).
findings.expected: An app→extension stop channel: the extension observes a stop Darwin note (or polls a stop flag in state.json on each buffer) and calls finishBroadcastWithError / finalizes and writes result.json with USER_STOPPED; the app waits (bounded) for result.json before resolving.
findings.rootCause: The extension side of the stop handshake was never implemented; the app-side comment (:98-99) assumes it exists.
findings.remediation: In SampleHandler.broadcastStarted register a Darwin observer for a dedicated stop name (not the 'finished' name the app itself listens to) that sets a flag; on the next buffer finalize the segment, write result.json (USER_STOPPED/COMPLETE or the client limitation), and finishBroadcastWithError with a user-facing 'stopped from PROOVRA' message. In the module, wait up to N seconds for result.json before reading, and never synthesize startedAtUtc=now.
findings.requiredTests: Device acceptance: start broadcast, stop in-app → indicator disappears, result terminationReason USER_STOPPED, last segment emitted. Unit: a Swift-free JS test that the stop path waits for a result instead of accepting the fallback.

findings.title: Extension segment timing is wrong: the final segment is recorded with durationMs 0 and a start offset equal to the session end, so COMPLETE iOS sessions are refused as having an undeclared gap

findings.userImpact: Even with UC-IOS-001 fixed, a cleanly stopped session whose last segment is longer than 3 s (roughly half of all sessions at 6 s segments) fails Finish & Sign with CONTINUOUS_MANIFEST_INVALID. Static screens (ReplayKit delivers no new frames when nothing changes) also create >3 s wall-clock gaps between segments.
findings.legalImpact: The last segment's declared duration (0) is false provenance in the manifest.
findings.reproduction: broadcastFinished calls finalizeSegment(durationMs: 0, force: true) (SampleHandler.swift:74). finalizeSegment computes offsetMs = wallElapsed − durationMs (:121) = wallElapsed, and writes durationMs 0 (:126). With result COMPLETE_SESSION/USER_STOPPED (:75), the validator computes between = last.startedAtOffsetMs − (prev.startedAtOffsetMs + prev.durationMs) ≈ the true length of the last segment (:391); > maxGapMs 3000 (:73 of bounds) sets gapFound, and a COMPLETE session with a gap is refused (:402).
findings.observed: Final segment duration hard-coded to 0; offsets mix wall clock and PTS.
findings.expected: Final segment duration = last appended PTS − segmentStartPts; offsets derived from one clock (PTS relative to the first frame of the session).
findings.rootCause: finalizeSegment's force path passes a literal 0 instead of measuring the segment.
findings.remediation: Track lastPts; on force-finalize use lastPts − segmentStartPts; compute startedAtOffsetMs from segmentStartPts − sessionFirstPts. Record a limitation when a segment spans a long no-frame interval rather than letting it read as a gap.

Because of UC-IOS-002 the broadcast actually continues, but observing stops, so the rest is lost.
findings.legalImpact: Sessions are labelled with SEGMENT_UPLOAD_BACKPRESSURE and end at the moment the user came back, not when they stopped.
findings.reproduction: app.json ios.infoPlist (:51-69) declares no UIBackgroundModes; ReplayKit runs the extension in its own process while the host app is suspended within seconds of leaving foreground. Darwin posts from the extension are not processed by a suspended app. On resume, the next segmentReady note triggers drainSegments (ProovraScreenCaptureModule.swift:133-139) which emits all pending segments; onSegment (continuous-capture.tsx:153-176) evaluates shouldStopForBackpressure(captured, uploaded, maxPendingSegments=8).
findings.observed: Android-shaped streaming/backpressure policy applied unchanged to iOS.
findings.expected: iOS policy that treats the App Group container as the durable spool: no backpressure stop for a backlog that exists only because the app was suspended; upload on return / on stop; honest copy ('uploads when you return to PROOVRA').
findings.rootCause: Shared UC-3 client flow assumes the host process runs during capture, which is false on iOS.

Member B of the same team (evidence.create) calls POST /v1/uploads/sessions/<sid>/parts/0/presign {teamId} -> presignStorageUploadPart loads the session by (teamId, sessionId) only and returns an S3 part URL; B PUTs his bytes and calls /parts/0/uploaded with his ETag (markPartUploaded is team-scoped and COALESCEs client_sha256); B or A calls /multipart/complete -> completeStorageMultipart (team-scoped) -> bridge writeEvidencePart as principal session.actor_user_id (A). A's finalize hashes and signs B's bytes.
findings.observed: Only createUploadSession and abortUploadSession check actor/owner (ET-UPL-01/02); presign, parts/uploaded, multipart/initiate, multipart/complete and complete do not. RUNTIME: Same-workspace MEMBER: presign on the OWNER's session → 200; PUT → 200; parts/0/uploaded → 200; multipart/complete → 200 (serverSha256 = injected digest). evidence_parts row 0 of the owner's record now carries the member's digest and the multipart key. findings.expected: Every session mutation requires the caller to be the session's actor (or the record owner), answering like an unknown session otherwise.
findings.rootCause: ET-UPL-01 fix moved the bridge to the byte-write authority as the SESSION's actor, not the CALLER; per-route caller checks were added only to create/abort.
findings.remediation: Add actorUserId to presignStorageUploadPart/markPartUploaded/initiate/completeStorageMultipart/completeUploadSession inputs and require actor_user_id = caller in the loading query.
findings.requiredTests: Two members of one team; B's presign/uploaded/multipart-complete on A's session -> 404 session_not_found.

findings.title: Integrity checks compare stored bytes to unsigned columns (fileSha256 / EvidencePart.sha256); nothing binds them to the signed fingerprint, yet the UI calls it 'its signed hash'

greenTests: services/api/test/public-verify-stored-bytes-truth.integration.test.ts::TRUST-001: bytes and digest columns rewritten consistently (real MinIO)

findings.userImpact: A record whose bytes and digest columns were changed together keeps 'Stored file rechecked - matched its signed hash', a valid signature and a verified original on Verify.
findings.legalImpact: The platform's own recheck and verify answers would certify substituted evidence under an insider/DB-write threat model; the signed fingerprint that would expose the substitution is never consulted.
findings.securityImpact: Defence-in-depth gap: the signature protects fingerprintCanonicalJson, but every byte-level check reads mutable, unsigned columns of the evidence and evidence_parts tables (neither is append-only).
findings.reproduction: Signed multipart record R. As a DB writer: PUT new bytes to R's key (new S3 version), UPDATE evidence_parts SET sha256=<new>, storage_version_id=<new version>; UPDATE evidence SET file_sha256=sha256(join('|')), storage_version_id=... . Run the recheck: observeOriginalDigest computes the new composite and compares it to evidence.fileSha256 (integrity-recheck.ts:181-183) -> VERIFIED. Public Verify: canonicalHashMatches = sha256(fingerprintCanonicalJson)===fingerprintHash (evidence.routes.ts:13340-13344) and signatureValid over it -> both true; custody chain untouched -> valid. fingerprintCanonicalJson still lists the ORIGINAL part sha256 values and the UPLOAD_COMPLETED custody payload still holds the original fileSha256; no code compares either with the columns.
findings.observed: No verifier parses fingerprintCanonicalJson.file.sha256 / file.parts[].sha256 or the UPLOAD_COMPLETED payload and compares them with fileSha256 / EvidencePart.sha256 (grep: the only JSON.parse of the fingerprint is services/worker/src/report-v2/content-model.ts:41 for counts). The stored-bytes copy says 'matched its signed hash'.
findings.expected: The expected digest of every byte check is derived from (or asserted equal to) the signed fingerprint: single-file file.sha256, multipart composite of file.parts[].sha256 in partIndex order, with part storage coordinates from the fingerprint. A disagreement between the fingerprint and the columns is itself an integrity failure.
findings.rootCause: The fingerprint is treated as an opaque signed blob; fileSha256 and part sha256 columns were introduced as 'the' digest and every later reader trusts them.
findings.remediation: Add one shared resolver signedDigestsFromFingerprint(fingerprintCanonicalJson) and use it (a) as expectedDigest in observeOriginalDigest/recordIntegrityObservation, (b) in Public Verify / review workspace as a 'columnsMatchSignedFingerprint' check feeding overallIntegrity, (c) in report issuance before promotion. Treat a mismatch as FAILED_HASH_MISMATCH.
findings.requiredTests: Live-PG test: sign a record, rewrite file_sha256 + evidence_parts.sha256 + bytes consistently, assert recheck FAILED and Verify not verified; unit test for the resolver on single/multipart/legacy fingerprints.

findings.title: Darwin observer lifecycle is broken: each registration uses a throw-away NSObject pointer, removeAll never removes them, and drainSegments runs on two threads

resolution.externalProofRemaining: Swift unit test on macOS CI

findings.userImpact: Repeated sessions accumulate CF observers so each note triggers N drains/N stop events; a race between the Expo queue (stop) and main thread (Darwin callback) on lastEmittedSequence can emit a segment twice, leading to a failed duplicate upload toast or a duplicate partIndex that the validator refuses.
findings.legalImpact: none
findings.reproduction: observe() passes Unmanaged.passUnretained(NSObject()).toOpaque() (:202) — a new, immediately released object each call; removeAll() passes yet another new pointer (:211), which matches no registered observer. drainSegments (Module :133-139) is called from the AsyncFunction (:101) and from the Darwin callback on main (:117,:121) without synchronization.
findings.observed: Leaked observers; unsynchronized shared state.
findings.expected: One stable observer token (e.g. the module instance), removed with the same token; drain serialized on one queue.
findings.rootCause: Incorrect CFNotificationCenter observer identity.
findings.remediation: Use Unmanaged.passUnretained(self) of a long-lived object and serialize drainSegments on a DispatchQueue.
findings.requiredTests: Swift unit test (requires macOS CI).

findings.title: RFC 3161 trust configuration is unguarded: anchor/policy absent from env templates and readiness, production test-anchor refusal is a subject-string + NODE_ENV check, policy allow-list optional, genTime-unparsed tokens verified at 'now'

resolution.externalProofRemaining: A real production TSA chain validated end to end (external-proof-register row 2).; real TSA chain validation outside Production

findings.userImpact: A production deploy without TSA_TRUST_BUNDLE_PATH silently records every new timestamp as FAILED ('Timestamp failed') with no readiness signal; a mistakenly mounted non-marker CA bundle (e.g. a staging root) is accepted as a trust anchor.
findings.legalImpact: Low: all failures are fail-closed, but the positive path accepts any policy OID and any anchor the file contains.
findings.securityImpact: Anchor pinning relies solely on the mounted file; the test-anchor guard triggers only for subjects containing PROOVRA-TEST-TSA-ANCHOR and only when NODE_ENV === 'production' (PROOVRA_ENV not consulted).
findings.reproduction: grep TSA_TRUST_BUNDLE_PATH|TSA_ACCEPTED_POLICY_OIDS|tsa_trust_anchor_not_configured outside tests/docs: only validate-tsa-token.ts. .env.example files contain no TSA_* keys. With genTime unparsed (parse-tsa-reply.ts:384 warning) -attime is omitted (validate-tsa-token.ts:187) so signer validity is checked at the current time.
findings.observed: No boot/readiness/ops check for anchor or policy; TSA_USERNAME/PASSWORD mandatory even for unauthenticated TSAs (timestamp.service.ts:195-196), which throws and blocks completion.
findings.expected: Production readiness fails (or ops condition raised) when TSA_ENABLED without a readable non-test anchor and an accepted-policy list; anchor fingerprint allow-list; refuse STAMPED when genTime cannot be parsed; optional credentials.
findings.rootCause: ET-TSA-01 remediation fixed the validator but left configuration as documentation (docs/operations/external-proof-register.md).
findings.remediation: Add TSA config to secrets-authority/readiness, require TSA_ACCEPTED_POLICY_OIDS in production, pin expected anchor SHA-256, treat unparsed genTime as not validated, make credentials optional.
findings.requiredTests: Readiness test for missing anchor in production; validator test for unparsed genTime; production + PROOVRA_ENV test.
